card.does: Mild hydride. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol, ketone → 2° alcohol (the solvent supplies the proton).
card.doesNot: Leaves C=C, esters and carboxylic acids alone.

label: LiAlH₄
name: Lithium aluminium hydride (dry ether or THF)

card.does: Strong hydride. Aldehydes, ketones, acids and esters → metal alkoxides (an ester gives two). Opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Needs a separate H₂O / H₃O⁺ workup. Does not touch isolated C=C.

card.does: Reduces C=C to C–C and aldehyde/ketone C=O to the alcohol.
card.doesNot: Not used for esters, acids or benzene rings in this course.

card.does: Aldehyde/ketone C=O → CH₂.
card.doesNot: Does not reduce alcohols, esters or acids.

card.does: Aldehyde/ketone C=O → CH₂ (base conditions).
card.doesNot: Does not reduce alcohols, esters or acids.

card.does: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (stops there); 2° alcohol → ketone.
card.doesNot: Leaves C=C alone; no acids; does not cleave C–C bonds.

card.does: 1° alcohol → carboxylic acid; 2° alcohol → ketone; hydroquinone/catechol → quinone.
card.doesNot: 3° alcohols: no reaction. Never stops at the aldehyde.

card.does: Cleaves the C–C bond of a vicinal diol; each carbon becomes an aldehyde or ketone.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to an isolated alcohol or a 1,3-diol.

label: OsO₄
name: Osmium tetroxide, then NaHSO₃/H₂O (or cat. OsO₄ + NMO)

card.does: Syn dihydroxylation: two OH groups on the same face of a C=C. The C–C bond is kept.
card.doesNot: Does not cleave the C=C (that is O₃).

card.does: Step 1 of hydroboration: B and H add syn across the C=C, boron on the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Gives no alcohol by itself; follow with H₂O₂/NaOH.

card.does: Step 2 of hydroboration: swaps C–B for C–OH with retention.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to an alkene on its own.

card.does: Strong, unselective oxidant that cleaves C=C bonds.
card.trap: Not a toolkit reagent: use OsO₄ for diols, Jones or PCC for alcohols.

card.does: Cleaves C=C into two carbonyls.
card.trap: Decoy for OsO₄: OsO₄ keeps the C–C bond and gives a syn diol.

card.does: Alkene → epoxide (syn, stereospecific). Sulfide → sulfoxide (1 equiv) → sulfone (2 equiv).
card.doesNot: Not a diol reagent.

card.does: Sulfide → sulfoxide with 1 equiv, → sulfone with 2 equiv.
card.doesNot: Does not open epoxides or oxidise alcohols here.

card.does: Sulfide → sulfoxide, and stops there.
card.doesNot: Does not go on to the sulfone.

card.does: Oxidises two thiols to a disulfide RS–SR.
card.doesNot: Does not touch alcohols or alkenes here.

card.does: With light, peroxide or heat: allylic / benzylic bromination.
card.doesNot: Nothing happens in the dark without an initiator.

card.does: Protonates alkoxides, carboxylates and thiolates; quenches Grignards. With heat: Ar–N₂⁺ → Ar–OH.
card.doesNot: Does nothing useful before the hydride or Grignard has reacted.

card.does: Acidic workup: protonates alkoxides, phenoxides and carboxylates. On an epoxide: trans-diol. On an alkene: Markovnikov hydration.
card.doesNot: Kills a Grignard or hydride if added too early.

card.does: ROH → RBr (3° fast by SN1, 1° by SN2). Epoxide → bromohydrin at the more substituted carbon. Excess + heat: cleaves ethers to alkyl bromides (an aryl–O bond survives as the phenol).
card.trap: Light does nothing useful here; keep the lamp off.

card.does: Excess + heat: cleaves ethers to alkyl iodides; alkyl aryl ethers → phenol + RI.
card.doesNot: Never breaks the aryl–O bond.

card.does: 3° alcohol → 3° chloride (SN1).
card.doesNot: 1° and 2° alcohols need ZnCl₂ (Lucas) to react.

card.does: 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols → alkyl chlorides.
card.doesNot: Not an oxidant.

card.does: ROH → RCl.
card.doesNot: Not an oxidant or a reductant.

card.does: 1°/2° ROH → RBr by SN2, no rearrangement.
card.doesNot: Not for 3° alcohols.

card.does: Dehydration to the Zaitsev alkene (E1; 1° alcohols only at 180 °C). Two 1° alcohols at 140 °C → symmetric ether. 1,4- and 1,5-diols → cyclic ether.
card.doesNot: Not an oxidant.

card.does: Electrophilic nitration of benzene rings (not in this toolkit).
card.trap: Looks like NaNO₂ on a tired day. It is not the diazonium route.

card.does: Mononitrates a phenol ortho/para to the OH (para if open).
card.doesNot: Does not touch the OH group.

label: NaNO₂ / H₂SO₄
name: Sodium nitrite in sulfuric (or hydrochloric) acid

card.does: Makes HONO; at 0–5 °C converts Ar–NH₂ into the aryl diazonium salt Ar–N₂⁺.
card.doesNot: Not a nitrating agent. Warm, the diazonium salt decomposes.

card.does: Brominates every open ortho/para position of a phenol.
card.doesNot: Does not touch the OH.

card.does: Mono-brominates a phenol: para if open, otherwise ortho.
card.doesNot: Not polybromination.

card.does: Deprotonates phenols (pKa ≈ 10), thiols and carboxylic acids. Vicinal halohydrin → epoxide.
card.doesNot: Too weak to deprotonate an ordinary alcohol fully; does not replace NH₂ or OH on a ring.

card.does: Deprotonates carboxylic acids (and only very acidic phenols such as picric acid).
card.doesNot: Does not deprotonate an ordinary phenol or an alcohol.

card.does: Deprotonates phenols for a Williamson aryl ether synthesis.
card.doesNot: Too weak for ordinary alcohols.

card.does: Strong base: alcohol → alkoxide, phenol → phenoxide, thiol → thiolate (step 1 of a Williamson).
card.doesNot: Not a nucleophile and not a reducing agent.

card.does: Alcohol → alkoxide (with H₂ gas), like NaH.
card.doesNot: Not a nucleophile.

card.does: Fries rearrangement: aryl ester → ortho/para hydroxyaryl ketone.
card.trap: Not a base. It cannot make an alkoxide for a Williamson synthesis.

card.does: Alkyl / aryl halide → Grignard reagent R–MgBr.
card.doesNot: Destroyed by any acidic H (OH, SH, COOH, NH) in the molecule.

card.does: Kolbe–Schmitt: phenoxide + CO₂ → carboxylate ortho to the O⁻.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to a neutral phenol.

card.does: Perfect SN2 electrophile: alkylates alkoxides, phenoxides, thiolates and sulfides (→ sulfonium).
card.doesNot: Cannot be eliminated (no β-hydrogens).

card.does: 1° halide: SN2 electrophile for alkoxides, phenoxides and thiolates.
card.doesNot: Elimination is minor with a 1° halide.

card.does: 1° halide: SN2 electrophile.
card.doesNot: Elimination is minor with a 1° halide.

card.does: Benzylic 1° halide: excellent SN2 electrophile.
card.doesNot: No β-hydrogens next to the benzylic carbon, so no E2.

card.does: Allylic 1° halide: excellent SN2 electrophile.
card.doesNot: Its own C=C is untouched.

card.does: 2° halide: E2 with alkoxides (propene).
card.trap: Put the isopropyl group on the alkoxide side instead.

card.does: 3° halide: E2 with alkoxides (2-methylpropene).
card.trap: Never the electrophile in a Williamson ether synthesis.

card.does: Grignard partner: R–MgBr + HCHO → 1° alcohol with one extra carbon (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a Grignard or hydride.

card.does: Grignard partner: → 2° alcohol (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a Grignard or hydride.

card.does: Grignard partner: → 2° benzylic alcohol (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a Grignard or hydride.

card.does: Grignard partner: → 3° alcohol (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a Grignard or hydride.

card.does: Grignard partner: → 3° alcohol on the ring (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a Grignard or hydride.

card.does: Grignard partner: R–MgBr opens it → 1° alcohol with two extra carbons (after H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Nothing without a nucleophile.

card.does: Acylates alcohols and phenols on oxygen → acetate ester.
card.doesNot: No AlCl₃, so no ring acylation.

card.does: Acylates alcohols and phenols on oxygen → benzoate ester.
card.doesNot: No AlCl₃, so no ring acylation.

card.does: Acylates alcohols and phenols on oxygen → acetate ester.
card.doesNot: No AlCl₃, so no ring acylation.

label: CH₃COOH, H₂SO₄ cat., Δ
name: Acetic acid with catalytic sulfuric acid, heat (Fischer)

card.does: Fischer esterification: alcohol (the nucleophile) + acid → acetate ester + water.
card.doesNot: Phenols esterify poorly this way; use the acid chloride or anhydride.

card.does: With heat: Fischer esterification of a carboxylic acid → methyl ester. On an epoxide: methoxy goes to the MORE substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Does not esterify alcohols (needs an acid partner).

card.does: With heat: Fischer esterification of a carboxylic acid → ethyl ester. On an epoxide: ethoxy to the MORE substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Does not esterify alcohols.

card.does: C-acylation of a phenol ring ortho/para to the OH → hydroxyaryl ketone; the OH stays.
card.doesNot: Not O-acylation (no pyridine).

card.does: Alkoxide nucleophile: opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon; SNAr on aryl halides with NO₂ ortho/para.
card.doesNot: No reaction with a plain aryl halide (no SN2 on sp² carbon).

card.does: Alkoxide nucleophile: opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon; SNAr on activated aryl halides.
card.doesNot: No reaction with a plain aryl halide.

card.does: Cyanide nucleophile: opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Nothing on an alcohol.

card.does: Azide nucleophile: opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Nothing on an alcohol.

card.does: Opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon → amino alcohol.
card.doesNot: Nothing on an alcohol.

card.does: HS⁻ nucleophile: CH₃/1°/2° halide → thiol (SN2); opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Cannot displace OH: convert the alcohol to the bromide first.

card.does: Thiolate nucleophile: halide → sulfide (SN2); opens epoxides at the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Cannot displace OH.

card.does: 'Naked' fluoride: SN2 on a CH₃/1°/2° halide → alkyl fluoride.
card.doesNot: Nothing on alcohols.

card.does: 'Naked' cyanide: SN2 on a CH₃/1°/2° halide → nitrile.
card.doesNot: Nothing on alcohols.

card.does: 'Naked' acetate: SN2 on a CH₃/1°/2° halide → acetate ester.
card.doesNot: Nothing on alcohols.

card.does: Carbon nucleophile: opens an epoxide at the less substituted carbon → magnesium alkoxide (then H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Destroyed by acidic O–H / S–H / N–H in the flask.

card.does: Carbon nucleophile: opens an epoxide at the less substituted carbon → magnesium alkoxide (then H₃O⁺).
card.doesNot: Destroyed by acidic O–H / S–H / N–H in the flask.

card.does: Hydrates a C=C the Markovnikov way: H to the less substituted carbon, OH to the more substituted one (via the carbocation). Also opens epoxides to trans diols.
card.doesNot: No heat, so no dehydration; alcohols, ethers and carbonyls are untouched.

card.does: Alcohol → tosylate (ROTs). The C–O bond is kept (retention), and OTs is a halide-like leaving group for the next SN2/E2 step.
card.doesNot: Makes nothing else: a tosylate is the setup for substitution, not its product.

card.does: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (stops there); 2° alcohol → ketone. Chromium-free alternative to PCC.
card.doesNot: No carboxylic acids; 3° alcohols untouched; C=C left alone.

card.does: Like PCC: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (stops there); 2° alcohol → ketone.
card.doesNot: No acids; does not cleave C–C bonds.

label: t-BuOOH, Ti(OiPr)₄, (+)-DET
name: Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation (tert-butyl hydroperoxide, titanium(IV) isopropoxide, diethyl L-(+)-tartrate)

card.does: Epoxidises the C=C of an ALLYLIC alcohol only, giving one enantiomer (the tartrate picks the face).
card.doesNot: Isolated alkenes (no OH on the next carbon) are untouched.
